structure: Learner protest and pressure to continue
Participant may refuse; preserve the escalation and stop rule
outcome: Completion of the maximum step in an escalating compliance trajectory; not merely agreeing to one step.
domain: Corporate evaluator delivering escalating critical feedback under supervisor pressure (spec example).
equivalence_risks: Physical pain versus reputational discomfort changes stakes; not automatically equivalent
Cannot tell participant that harm is fake or that learner is a confederate
Single final-step vignette does not reproduce a maximum-voltage trajectory

structure: Unanimous incorrect peer answers before participant responds
Correct option and majority option counterbalanced without revealing that peers are scripted
outcome: Share of critical perceptual trials matching the incorrect majority; cluster repeated trials by participant.
domain: Product colour matching in a marketing setting (spec example).
equivalence_risks: Supplying the correct answer in prose changes a perception task into an instruction conflict
Colour and line judgments need controlled stimuli and competence checks
A single hypothetical response is not the original repeated-critical-trial measure

structure: Responder acceptance implements split; rejection pays both zero
Role decisions isolated to avoid contamination from answering the other role
outcome: Keep proposer offer share separate from responder acceptance at each offered share; do not infer a rejection threshold from one offer.
equivalence_risks: Workplace entitlement or recurring relationships may change the payoff game
Hypothetical points lack real monetary incentives
Primary 20-percent offer alone cannot test proposer distribution or equal-offer acceptance

actors: person at risk or incident source
structure: Same observable emergency and same opportunity to help
Manipulate whether other helpers are present without implying that they already acted
Keep danger, intervention cost, knowledge and time window fixed in a presence contrast
outcome: Intervention within a defined observation window, distinguishing individual helping from whether any member of a group helps.
equivalence_risks: Smoke/pluralistic ignorance and seizure/diffusion of responsibility are different procedures
Risk to people versus software reliability changes stakes
A model statement of intent is not timed human intervention

structure: An explicit removal/threat versus a comparable no-threat condition
Specified preference measurement before/after where required
Measure restoration separately from simple inability to select the removed option
outcome: Threat-versus-control change in preference or adjacent-option selection; define adjacency and response denominator before conversion to a binary rate.
equivalence_risks: Ranking shifts, anger and binary selection are different outcomes
A standardized mean difference cannot specify a unique probability difference without distribution and base-rate assumptions
Removal changes feasible options; compare against a carefully matched control
